{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABYj6LNA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhCIwJM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 11, "title": "Expand WonderSwan hardware compatibility: cartridge saves/mappers, CPU/interrupts, color video, and audio", "body": "## Problem

The current Rust/WebAssembly emulator has a small, intentionally limited hardware subset. A ROM can be rejected during cartridge-header validation with the generic error `Unsupported save hardware, mapper, or cartridge flags.`, even if its file is structurally valid. Accepting the header would not fix execution: cartridge save memory, additional mapper behavior, many V30MZ instructions, interrupts/timers, color graphics, sprites, and sound are still missing.

The goal is to implement these **hardware features generically**, based on public hardware documentation and independent tests—not to make an exception for a specific ROM, publisher, game, or file hash. The resulting code should improve compatibility across independently authored programs while preserving the already working original demo.

**Do not add, upload, bundle, publish, commit, or download any commercial game ROM, proprietary BIOS/boot ROM, or unlicensed game content.** The implementation and acceptance tests must be self-contained using original synthetic fixtures/homebrew source generated within the repository.

## Expected outcome

The emulator can parse valid cartridge configurations with common battery-backed save devices, support Bandai 2001 and 2003 mapper functionality relevant to those configurations, execute a substantially broader set of V30MZ/80186 instructions with hardware interrupt/timer handling, render the WonderSwan Color hardware's tile/sprite/palette modes, and produce basic WonderSwan audio through Web Audio. The same reusable Rust hardware core supports WonderSwan (mono), WonderSwan Color, and SwanCrystal (default); models must differ according to documented capabilities rather than being three names for the same monochrome renderer.

This issue is a **hardware-compatibility milestone**, not a guarantee that every commercial cartridge will work. Clearly document implemented and unimplemented behavior instead of inventing support or bypassing ROM-header checks.

## Context and implementation guidance

Current relevant code (inspect again when implementing):

- `crates/ws-core/src/cartridge.rs` currently accepts only power-of-two ROMs of 128 KiB–4 MiB and rejects any nonzero save-type or mapper header byte and several flags in one combined error.
- `crates/ws-core/src/bus.rs` returns `0xFF` for the cartridge save-memory region `0x10000..=0x1FFFF`, does not implement a working RAM bank register, and exposes only a small set of I/O ports.
- `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs` implements a subset of 80186 instructions and returns explicit errors on unsupported instructions. There is no interrupt delivery. `crates/ws-core/src/lib.rs` runs a CPU instruction at a simplified fixed four-cycle cost.
- `crates/ws-core/src/video.rs` renders only monochrome, 2bpp Screen 1 tiles. Screen 2, sprites, windows, color tile formats, and color palettes are not implemented.
- `crates/ws-web` and `web/` already provide Wasm, local ROM loading, controls, an original demo, and GitHub Pages publication. Keep their game-first UI and `/wonderswan-rust/` public asset base.
- The project implements its emulator core from scratch; **do not port/copy/vendor an existing emulator**. Hardware descriptions and public test specifications may be consulted.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/AGENTS.md), the [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md). Use English for collaboration and clearly separate pre-merge versus post-merge verification.

Useful independent hardware references: [ROM header](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/ROM_header), [memory map](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Memory_map), [mapper](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Mapper), [Bandai 2001](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Bandai_2001), [Bandai 2003](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Bandai_2003), [CPU](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/NEC_V30MZ), [interrupts](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Interrupts), [timers](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Timers), [display](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Display), [palette](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Display/Palette), [tile data](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Display/Tile_Data), [sprites](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Display/Sprites), [sound](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Sound).

### Implementation requirements

**A. Cartridge header, mapper, and save devices**

- Decode each header field into a named, typed representation, and validate ROM size/checksum, hardware model restrictions, save type, flags, and mapper capability **independently**. Invalid combinations must yield distinct actionable errors including the unsupported field/value; never silently bypass or rewrite the header.
- Support common documented **SRAM sizes including 32 KiB**, with correct `0x10000..=0x1FFFF` addressing, bank selection via `0xC1`, mirroring/bounds, 8-bit reads/writes, initialization, and distinction between volatile RAM and battery-backed cartridge memory. Do not make SRAM read-only or return permanent `0xFF` on writes.
- Implement the documented external cartridge **EEPROM** save protocol for supported documented sizes/commands and status, as distinct from SRAM. Keep any unsupported save types rejected with explicit reasons.
- Support shared Bandai 2001 / Bandai 2003 banking via `0xC0..=0xC3`, plus the necessary **2003-specific** register behavior (including `0xCA..=0xCF` where applicable: RTC status/payload, GPO, self-flash mapping and extended ROM banking). Implement a documented subset with tests for each recognized operation; do not silently treat recognized operations as no-ops or assume ROM header bytes directly identify the physical chip without verifying the documented format. Any flash-writing or unsupported RTC/board feature must be represented accurately or rejected explicitly. Retain the existing no-save ROM behavior.
- Expose nonvolatile cartridge save data through a minimal **browser-local** persistence mechanism keyed by a robust identity of the loaded ROM (for example, a content digest, not just a filename). Save data must survive page reload/reopen and remain isolated between different ROMs; provide safe import/export if that is simpler for user control, but automatic persistence is required. Keep persistence in the frontend adapter and browser only; no game-data upload or server storage. Do not accidentally erase saves on model change, pause, or ordinary reset.
- Keep ROM size, mapper and cartridge capability enforcement grounded in the documented hardware. If extending supported ROM sizes beyond the current range is necessary for documented bank behavior, implement and test their mapping rather than merely lifting input-size limits.

**B. CPU, interrupt controller, and timing**

- Expand generic NEC V30MZ/80186 instruction support substantially beyond the demo subset, covering at least rotates/shifts, MUL/IMUL/DIV/IDIV (with zero/overflow faults), more arithmetic/flag/decimal and string variants, far CALL/RET and related control flow, and INT/INTO/IRET with correct stack/flags/segment effects. Handle documented prefix, ModR/M, segment, and carry/overflow semantics. Explicitly document any remaining instruction gaps; never coerce an unknown instruction to NOP.
- Implement maskable interrupt delivery including IF, interrupt vector lookup, priority/request/enable/acknowledgement via the documented controller ports, and `HLT` wake-up when an eligible interrupt occurs. Handle display line match and VBlank events, plus HBlank/VBlank programmable timer behavior, using a shared timebase.
- Replace the unconditional four-cycles-per-instruction approximation with an instruction/bus-aware cycle accounting scheme sufficiently accurate for timer and scanline tests, including deterministic frame progression. It need not be perfect at subpixel-level, but cannot treat every instruction as having the same cost.
- Keep the firmware-free initialization path explicit and documented; **do not** include any proprietary boot ROM. Preserve reasonable reproducibility while identifying behavior that depends on unimplemented boot-firmware initialization.

**C. Video for all three models**

- Retain the 224×144 Rust-owned framebuffer and monochrome rendering compatibility.
- Implement Screen 1 and Screen 2 composition, tile maps, scrolling and window handling; the hardware sprite layer with sprite priority, flipping, palette selection, scanline limits, and window behavior; documented transparency/priority rules.
- Add the documented WonderSwan Color **2bpp and 4bpp** tile layouts (planar and packed where selected by the hardware), VRAM layout, color-palette RAM, palette transparency, and 12-bit RGB output, while preserving mono mode behavior and proper model gating. Treat SwanCrystal as a color-capable model, not a third graphics architecture requiring a different core.
- Rendering updates must come from actual emulated memory/ports/time progression, not hardcoded screenshots or ROM-specific patterns. Accurate LCD response/ghosting simulation is not a requirement.

**D. Audio**

- Add basic documented **four-channel WonderSwan sound** generation (wavetable plus relevant voice/sweep/noise modes) from emulated register writes, and deliver playable samples to the browser via Web Audio without changing the CPU core into a browser-dependent library.
- Implement a bounded audio buffer / sample clock, handle pause/reset/visibility safely, and preserve silent output when nothing is playing. Advanced color-only Hyper Voice and DMA can be documented as unsupported if not implemented, but must not be falsely reported as implemented.

**E. Validation fixtures and integration**

- Create small **original, generated-from-source, freely redistributable** cartridge fixtures/programs to verify independently: (1) SRAM/EEPROM reads, writes and banked persistence; (2) both mapper variants and bank boundaries; (3) CPU arithmetic/control flow/interrupt/timer events; (4) BG2, sprites and color modes; (5) sound register operation and non-silent audio output. A few focused fixtures may share a build pipeline; do not need to create a polished game.
- Use a documented, freely redistributable license for fixture source, generated binary and assets, and include provenance. Do not commit, bundle, or download any commercial ROM, proprietary firmware or third-party copyrighted game assets. Loading privately owned ROMs locally remains a user action outside the test suite.
- Keep the existing original playable demo working across all three selectable models and preserve local ROM loading, model switching, pause/reset behavior, debug UI and GitHub Pages builds.
- Extend `docs/hardware-subset.md` (or an equivalent up-to-date hardware support document) with an exact per-component support matrix and known limitations; update README/UI messages accordingly. No blanket promise of broad commercial-ROM compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] ROM validation returns **separate diagnostic errors** identifying unsupported save type, mapper, flags, size, model, or checksum; acceptance of an otherwise valid supported save-bearing header is backed by memory/protocol tests, not just a relaxed condition.
- [ ] SRAM **including 32 KiB**, RAM bank selection, correct reads/writes/mirroring and saves that persist across a browser reload work, with tests for isolation between ROM identities, reset/model switching, and no network upload.
- [ ] Supported cartridge EEPROM variants have command/read/write/status unit tests; both shared mapper banking and the implemented Bandai 2003 extension registers have documented register-level tests. Undocumented/unimplemented operations remain identifiable rather than silently accepted.
- [ ] CPU tests cover each newly supported instruction family, flag effects, divide/interrupt faults, INT/IRET stack return, maskable-interrupt priority/acknowledgement, HLT wake-up, and HBlank/VBlank timer triggering. Instruction accounting and frame/scanline tests prove that not every instruction consumes the same constant four cycles.
- [ ] Native framebuffer tests generated from emulated tile, palette and sprite memory verify Screen 1/2 layering, scroll, window/priority rules, sprite limits, 2bpp/4bpp modes, and 12-bit color output. Mono and color model restrictions are tested.
- [ ] Audio tests confirm register writes produce deterministic non-silent samples (and silence when disabled); the browser can initialize, pause, resume and reset audio without leaking loops or crashing when audio is unavailable.
- [ ] At least one **self-authored cartridge integration fixture** exercises CPU execution → mapper/interrupt/input → video and (where relevant) save/audio effects. The baseline playable demo still passes its existing completion/restart tests in all three models.
- [ ] Rust formatting, tests, Clippy, Wasm compilation, TypeScript/production build and existing browser smoke tests pass. Add browser smoke checks for save persistence and the new graphics/audio capabilities using only licensed fixtures, and report actual results and any unavailable checks honestly.
- [ ] Documentation lists the precise supported save types, mapper operations, CPU instructions, interrupts/timers, video modes, audio modes, and remaining limitations. Error messages are useful without requiring developer tools; detailed diagnostics remain available in Debug Mode.
- [ ] Changes remain based on the existing Rust core + thin Wasm adapter and game-first frontend. No existing emulator is ported, no proprietary ROM/firmware or unlicensed asset is added, and no unrelated framework/refactor is introduced.

This is intentionally **one source Issue** for the hardware-compatibility milestone. Incremental implementation commits or reviewable sub-PRs are fine, but **do not mark the Issue completed** while any mandatory acceptance criterion remains unresolved. Do not fake test results with ROM-specific code paths.

## Optional validation

- Compare independent open hardware test vectors or appropriately licensed homebrew programs with an actual device or other independent observations if available. Physical-console access and unredistributable game software are not mandatory.
- Investigate later improvements to RTC accuracy, special flash cartridges, general/sound DMA, Hyper Voice, serial/UART, and LCD color-response simulation in future Issues when they are separately justified.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** Verify that the existing `main` GitHub Pages workflow builds/deploys successfully; record the run URL and result.
2. **Pending:** Open the public emulator and test a legally redistributable self-authored ROM/fixture with cartridge save operations, color rendering and sound without using or publishing any commercial ROM. Verify local save data survives a reload and that Debug Mode/error recovery still work.

Only live deployed-site verification belongs here; all code, test, local-browser and artifact checks above are pre-merge gates.
